title: FlashNext overall inference benchmark

checkpoints.title: Hot-expert and MTP foundation
checkpoints.detail: Local fork state before the adaptive-KV merge. Context only; no standalone timing row is attributed to this commit.

checkpoints.title: Raymond Huang: shared phase arena
checkpoints.detail: Imported adaptive KV streaming: host-backed KV, resident pages, and compute/KV arena repartition between prefill and decode.

checkpoints.title: Qwen4Exp streaming integration
checkpoints.detail: Hybrid indexer integration, sparse host-row gathering, tiled prefill, and arena reservation handling. Code-state checkpoint for the short sweep and first six fiction-scifi variants.

checkpoints.title: Resident KV for sparse attention
checkpoints.detail: Sparse attention reads resident KV from VRAM, uses host fallback outside the resident prefix, and reuses mirrored writes and invalidation. Tested with the 54-slot / 1-insert / 1-staging fiction-scifi variant.

checkpoints.title: Speculative streaming (local changes; base commit)
checkpoints.detail: Uncommitted multi-token verification, direct quantized KV reads, and sparse query-union gathering. Per-case source hashes identify the tested state.

checkpoints.title: Strata v0.1.13
checkpoints.detail: Official release engine; automatic prefill, expert cache, MTP and suffix lookup. Q2 and INT8 KV results are configuration comparisons.

notes: All runs configure 262144-token capacity and Q8_0 K/V. Actual inputs are about 2.1K tokens for short tests and 305 tokens for fiction-scifi; this is not full-256K throughput.
Short tests record a first request and a second request after startup. Warm means the second request; recorded prompt-cache reuse is zero. OS file-cache warmth is not controlled.
Fiction-scifi uses one fresh-server request and 20480 generated tokens. Its prefill measurement is a cold-start observation, not comparable to warm short-test prefill.

Identical prompts and sampling settings produced different generated sequences. The 54-slot host-gather and resident-KV runs first diverge at output token 1779. Single observations do not isolate every source of variation.

Peak GPU usage is total-device usage, including desktop and other allocations, sampled every two seconds across startup and inference. Brief spikes can be missed. CPU-only GPU usage is background device usage.
RAM usage is process working set (RSS), not virtual address space or total mappings. WDDM shared usage includes mapped host weights; its absolute value is not proof of VRAM spill.
Expert slot counts include staging. Resident experts per layer equal slots minus staging. Missing staging fields in older recordings use the verified default of two.
The microbatch 2048 and 4096 variants use an 8192 MiB arena; other streaming variants use 4000 MiB. Microbatch comparisons therefore also change arena size.
The first output token is excluded from decode interval deltas. Each sustained run has 20 intervals covering 20479 token-to-token steps.

Checkpoint hashes identify corresponding source states, not exact original binary identities. Early measurements used uncommitted integration work; later commits captured that work. Native and CPU runs used the same integration build with streaming disabled.
SSD throughput, pagefile residency, energy consumption, and full memory-allocation breakdowns were not recorded per variant. They are not inferred here.
These are throughput measurements. No generated text or quality score is included.

The _pciegen3x16 variant repeats the resident-KV 54-slot case after widening the PCIe link. It retains the same prompt, 20480-token target, 53 resident experts plus one staging slot, insertion limit, CPU threads and context. Expert hit/miss histories do not measure upload latency.

Shared-head MTP follow-up uses 262144 context, Q8 target and draft KV, 13/15 CPU threads, and the same fiction-scifi prompt. Short fit checks precede 20480 output tokens. Arena and expert slots differ to accommodate the drafter; these are configuration comparisons, not an isolated MTP speedup.
Overall report includes all recorded Strata Q2 and llama.cpp Q2 attempts, alongside original IQ4_XS CPU and GPU sweeps. Fit failures and user-stopped runs remain visible.

Strata expert slots are global across layers; llama.cpp slots are per layer and include staging. They are not directly comparable counts. Short Q2 checks use 305 input and 512 output tokens and have cold measurements only.
Q2 and IQ4_XS, INT8 and Q8_0 KV, draft policies, resident budgets, and sampling differ. Compare configuration settings before attributing a speed difference to an engine.
Greedy Q2 runs developed short repeating loops. Recommended non-thinking runs avoided those loops but both restarted their narratives. Measured token throughput is not a quality score.
Strata interval timings use client token arrival times; llama.cpp intervals use server timings. Elapsed graphs exclude loading and PLE preloading. No extrapolation beyond measured output.

PLE RAM tests lock about 26.8 GiB of a shared file mapping in a helper process. Engine RAM peaks exclude the helper; shared pages must not be counted twice. Total physical use can be inferred only from recorded system available RAM.

Strata maximum MTP window 4 includes the current token, so it corresponds to 3 proposals; suffix window 6 corresponds to 5 proposals. Recommended llama.cpp repeat disables lookup; recommended Strata run retains it.

pcie_comparison.note: Hits and misses measure expert-cache routing, not uploaded bytes or transfer latency. The completed 20480-token repeat improved average decode by 7.5% and prefill by 4.7%; cache hit rate was 57.1% versus 57.0%. Requests matched, but generated sequences differed, so this is not a perfectly controlled hardware comparison.
